instrument: FILL IN: <set name> (clone) / selected Drum Rack pads and instrument tracks
capture_track: FILL IN: index of the reused capture audio track
candidates: FILL IN: list of {source_track_index, drum_pad_note (or null), job, instrument_slug, midi_note, velocity, note_duration_beats, bounce_beats} chosen by hand per research/live-oneshot-pack.md section 1-2

trigger.mechanism: one session-clip note per one-shot, fired once, tapped via the same input-routing capture used by code/run_sweep_stem.py
trigger.note_duration_beats: short for percussive jobs (kick/rumble/hat_closed/hat_open/clap/perc/stab), long/held for sustained jobs (pad/riser/impact) -- set per instrument, not a single constant
trigger.bounce_beats: note_duration_beats plus enough tail to capture full decay; err long, trim later

purpose: Give the listening test a pool of real one-shot stimuli (Anthony's own racks) to sit alongside the synthetic out/sweeps stimuli, and check both against the measured real-one-shot distribution.
hypothesis: Renders from Anthony's own instruments should land inside the real p10-p90 bands in out/library_real.csv for their assigned job on attack_ms, decay_ms, crest_factor_db, spectral_centroid_hz, band_sub_share and band_high_share, by construction (they are real drum-rack/instrument renders, not synthetic approximations). A render that falls outside is worth a second listen: mislabelled job, a capture artifact, or a genuine real outlier worth keeping.
sidecar_note: sample_rate is read from the bounced wav file after the copy, not queried from Live. ambiguous_label is only present when the job assignment was a judgment call worth flagging.

restore.session_clip: delete the temporary one-note clip after each capture (optional on a disposable clone)

post_render_check.run_from: sound-function repo root, on the analysis machine, after copying the pack's wavs into out/sweeps/ (realism_check.py hardcodes that input path, no --dir flag)
post_render_check.reads: out/library_real.csv (real one-shot distributions, split by job)

ownership: These are Anthony's own renders of his own instruments. He owns them outright and may publish or redistribute them freely, unlike corpus stems from other producers (see research/stems-request.md) or Demucs-separated audio from released tracks, which must never be redistributed.
reuses_mechanism: code/run_sweep_stem.py (ensure_capture_track / bounce_stem), adapted to fire one MIDI note per one-shot instead of a repeating pattern
